title: Forgiveness settles into lasting peace
subtitle: Raag Sorath · Ang 628
summary: The shabad begins with the Perfect Guru's completed work: forgiveness given, peace found. It opens wider into peace spreading everywhere and comes to rest in singing the Guru's Bani and meditating on Naam.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who has tasted relief but does not yet know how to live from it. Stayed with, it keeps peace from becoming a passing feeling and turns it into praise, devotion, and a different atmosphere.
takeaway: Remember this: received forgiveness becomes lasting peace when it ripens into Naam.

lines.translation: The Perfect Guru has done it perfectly.
I have found lasting peace and bliss.
Everywhere, the people dwell in peace. ||1||
Devotional worship to the Lord is what gives rewards.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਿ ਪੂਰੈ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰਿ ਦੀਨੀ ਵਿਰਲੈ ਕਿਨ ਹੀ ਜਾਤੀ ॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur poorai kirapaa kar dheenee viralai kin hee jaatee || rahaau ||
lines.translation: The Perfect Guru, by His Grace, gave it to me; how rare are those who know this. ||Pause||
Sing the Word of the Guru's Bani, O Siblings of Destiny.
That is always rewarding and peace-giving.
Nanak has meditated on the Naam, the Name of the Lord.
He has realized his pre-ordained destiny. ||2||17||81||

structure: First, it starts with the Guru's forgiveness as a finished gift, not a tentative possibility.
Then, it lets that peace widen until it changes the whole atmosphere around the heart.
Finally, it ends by fastening lasting peace to Bani, praise, and meditated Naam.
